answer: A lotus can have many petals, but each agent identity should lock a modest bond through a random audit window. Independent peers review signed work and shared-control evidence before any forfeiture. A sable cluster of aliases ties up capital per identity, while a cipher-backed audit trail makes collusion harder to hide. This raises mass-Sybil costs, but wealthy attackers can still pay and false matches can exclude newcomers; keep bonds small and allow appeals.
